title: Dispatch: facts read from the text alone can be fitted from neighbouring pages; the pictures cannot
statement: A pending attack replays R-017's own lines in a random block order, so its drifting tables no longer follow the sections; on the practice split F-018 still holds (0.97 bits against 1.11 in book order), which says the section fact is met by any vocabulary that changes along the text and adds little beyond F-009 until a null keeps pages whole. The general lesson: every fact on the record is measured from the text alone, and a procedure fitted on public pages lying between the hidden ones can copy any such local statistic, so new text facts should be judged by whether a drifting chain could copy them before anyone registers them. The blue team now has a fair test of its own: declare a constructed language and run it against every fact (P-G-006), with pinned constructed-language references (P-J-004), which asks the opposite question to G-every-fact. Anchors remain the part of the record no generator can reach, but the first replication of Tucker and Talbert's herbal identifications recovered 2 of 9 genera blind, and both hits were folios whose identifications are widely published, so the masked protocol needs annotators screened for exposure (P-L4-005). Grid keys keep failing (79 of 79); new cells should wait until a calibration step shows the search has power there.
check: None: a dispatch. Counts as on /desk/brief at the time of writing (2026-11-25): 17 facts established, 2 refuted, 15 attacks succeeded, 79 keys failed; the block-order attack is branch R-attack-F-018-fleet-opus, the annotator report P-L4-005.
